newsitem.title: JAMAICA: More layoffs in Jamaica bauxite industry - Institute.
newsitem.headline: More layoffs in Jamaica bauxite industry - Institute.

text.p: The state-run Jamaica Bauxite Institute Monday announced that Jamaica's four bauxite companies plan to shed a total of 480 jobs this year, as the country finds itself competing for capital needed to upgrade old plants.
Just last week, two companies said they were letting go a total of 350 workers, despite the fact that bauxite and alumina production is at its highest levels since 1981.

The problem stems in part from a fall in world aluminium prices. The London Metals Exchange cash price dropped 19.6 percent in 1995 and fell a further 11.45 percent in the first nine months of this year.
Dennis Morrison, senior director at the JBI, said changes in the structure of the international firms has also played a role in the downsizing.

"The companies are converting their plants into business units, or profit centers," he said. "It is on the basis of efficiency that the companies will decide which plants to expand... plants have to compete with each other for the investment dollar."
He said the challenge for Jamaica is to modernize. The oldest plant, Alcan's Kirkvine, is 44 years old while the newest, Alcoa's Jamalco, was built 24 years ago.

In December last year, general manager at Alumina Partners (Alpart) Gene Miller warned that of the 60-odd alumina plants world-wide, Jamaica's were the least efficient in terms of employees to metric tons of alumina produced.
Alcan has set itself the target of producing 1,400 tons per employee by the end of the decade--it now produces 1,000 tons per worker.

Jamaica's decision to shift emphasis to alumina production saw exports climbing from 1.5 million metric tons in 1988 to just over 3 million tons last year, while bauxite exports have held steady at around 3.5 million tons per annum.

Despite the fall in world prices, the JBI said it anticipates earnings for 1996 should equal last year's. The sector brought in US$713.2 million in gross earnings and US$298.1 million in net earnings.

However, as a result, Morrison said Brazil is likely to surpass Jamaica as the world's third-largest bauxite producer this year, although the country will retain it's number three ranking for alumina production.
